title: Proximal Humerus and Clavicle Fractures
case: An 80-year-old has a fracture after tripping. What else must be addressed?
plan: Phase 1 (about 0 to 3 weeks): protect, control pain, keep the hand, elbow and neck moving, early gentle shoulder movement as allowed.

differentials.name: Shoulder dislocation
differentials.key: Squared-off shoulder, arm held fixed, mechanism

qa: Why move the elbow and hand from day 1? They stiffen quickly and are not at risk from the fracture.
Which nerve is most at risk with proximal humerus fractures? Axillary nerve: check deltoid and lateral arm sensation.
Why do pendulum exercises use body sway? To move the shoulder passively without active muscle pull across the fracture.
An 80-year-old has a fracture after tripping. What else must be addressed? Falls prevention and bone health.
Pain and deformity increase at week 3. What do you do? Stop exercises and contact the surgical team for imaging.

redFlags.Finding: Cold, pale hand, weak or absent pulse
New or worsening numbness or weakness
Increasing pain and deformity during rehabilitation
Fracture after trivial force with weight loss or cancer history

manual.name: Glenohumeral glides (grades I to II then III to IV)
manual.why: After healing confirmed with persistent stiffness

manual.name: Thoracic and cervical mobilisation
manual.finding: Reduces associated neck and upper back pain

exercise.Exercise: Hand squeezes, wrist and elbow range

exercise.Steps: Lean forward, support on a table, let the arm hang and sway in small circles by moving the body
Lie down, use the other hand to lift the arm overhead
Use a stick or slide hand on a table

exercise.Exercise: Active elevation, isometric then band rotator cuff work

modalityNotes: Ice for pain early; heat before stretching later. Other modalities not routinely needed.
pathway: Phase 1 (about 0 to 3 weeks): protect, control pain, keep the hand, elbow and neck moving, early gentle shoulder movement as allowed.
Phase 3 (from about 6 to 12 weeks): strength, function, return to activity.
Bone health referral and falls prevention for older adults.
Timelines vary with fracture type and surgery; follow medical guidance.
